Pope Leo marks US anniversary with migrant appeal

Pope Leo has used his first key address to the US to praise the country's history of welcoming migrants, urging Americans to live up to ideals of freedom and equality. The Pope's comments come as the US celebrates its 250th anniversary of independence from Britain. Pope Leo's visit to Lampedusa, an Italian island in the Mediterranean, has been seen as a symbol of his commitment to protecting migrants. The Pope's words have been interpreted as a rebuke to Trump's policies on immigration.
